title: West Milford's Clinton Road named nation's most haunted road for third year

content:
West Milford’s Clinton Road, for a third consecutive year, ranks as the most haunted road in the United States and now worldwide, according to Sixt.com, the official website of the international mobility service provider for rentals and reservations.

The desolate 10-mile-plus twisting span runs from Route 23 near Newfoundland to its northern end at Warwick Turnpike, Upper Greenwood Lake. The dense woodlands and tree-lined reservoirs add to the rural daytime beauty, especially with Fall foliage, yet cast a natural canopy that blocks nighttime moonlight—with no streetlights, it’s pitch dark and intimidating.

Adjacent to mostly undeveloped watershed property and state forest, Clinton Road has few homes and businesses along its span. The once-rough and -rocky narrow two-lane dirt road is now paved with asphalt. It’s a smooth ride for motorists and cyclists but worth keeping eyes wide open for anyone and anything, including wildlife crossings.

Hikers and naturalists enjoy perusing the woods and established trails and finding solitude. The 424-acre Clinton Reservoir is popular among boaters and anglers for smallmouth and largemouth bass and chain pickerel.

Ghosts, ghouls and folklore

Clinton Road congers up tales of the paranormal, including a young boy’s ghost said to haunt the waters beneath the bridge at dead man’s curve. Toss a coin into the water and it may bounce back to you, some say—the growing number of coins on the stream bed suggests that folks still test the myth.

Legend cites strange creatures and gatherings of witches, satanists and the occult as well as druids. Some say the surrounding woods contain disposed of bodies. On May 18, 1983, the body of a man identified as Daniel Deppner was found wrapped in a green garbage bag on the roadside by a passing cyclist.

There are residents and curious out-of-towners who claim to have seen phantom headlights that follow them while driving at night before quickly vanishing. The remnants of Clinton Furnace and Cross Castle remain popular among visitors and lurking youngsters.

The 2019 horror film “Clinton Road” has a firefighter unraveling the mystery of his wife’s disappearance on the byway. Weird NJ magazine devoted an entire issue to the legend.

A road less traveled

Jerry Somma, who lives near Clinton Road, frequently hikes the thoroughfare which he finds to be tranquil and safe.

“I’ve run across bears and wildlife, not much else that would cause concern,” Somma said. “The road can be dangerous and spooky at night, so you have to be cautious.”

A teacher in Bergen County, Somma believes the lore complements the aesthetics of the area, especially during this time of year, Halloween.

“The legend adds to the charm of the area,” he said. “People are aware and curious of the stories. My students ask me about it, usually with the question: ‘Have you ever seen anything unusual’? My answer is ‘no’.

“I’ve had students, 17- and 18-year-old kids, who drive up here for recreation. I advise them to drive safely. Be careful. Yet the likelihood of them seeing anything unusual is rare. A few rough turns and blind spots, that’s the scariest thing.”

Ahead of Halloween on Sunday, Oct. 18, the first Zombie Run took place on Clinton Road. The event, which benefited West Milford’s Junior Highlanders Track Club, was sold out with 500 runners and walkers, many donning costumes for the occasion.

“Clinton Road is the perfect place for a Zombie Run,” Neil Balestrieri, who co-created the event with fellow local resident, Brian Lesley; both are Junior Highlanders board member.

“The Zombie Run brings something new to Clinton Road and West Milford,” Balestrieri said. “It’s about keeping people healthy and benefiting our youngsters. Lots of scary costumes and participants having lots of fun—but nothing haunting.

“The legend is just that, some incredible stories. People should get to know Clinton Road and continue to tell and embrace the legend. It’s part of the West Milford story. Who knows, maybe we’ll encounter something spooky in the future, but I’m holding my breath.”

As for Halloween, there’s little trick-or-treating along Clinton Road. But for those interested in a spooky adventure, consider a visit and let your imagination run wild.
